Latin word

testimōnium

testimōnium, testimōniī n.

noun, second declension

evidence, testimony (of a witness)

In this lexicon

  • evidence

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Brut. 293: quam sī testimōnium dīcerēmus; Ter. Ph. 293: neque testimōnī dictiō est; Traupman 195, 311

  • testimōnium dīcere: witness

    classical

Examples

  • vidē nē religiō nōbīs tam adhibenda sit quam sī testimōnium dīcerēmus

    take care: we may need to be as scrupulous as if we were giving evidenceCic. Brut. 293

    In the entry for evidence

  • tum quī testimōnium dīceret ut arbitrārī sē dīceret etiam quod ipse vīdisset

    and that a witness should say “I think” even of what he had seen himselfCic. Ac. 2.146

    In the entry for evidence

  • Hoc testimōnium nōn sūmendum est.

    This evidence is not admissible.Traupman 195
